newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end up, 2nd Board near all-time high.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end up, 2nd Board near all-time high.

text.p: Second board stocks continued to shine, with the index almost hitting a new all-time high before closing just below it.
Heavyweight stocks were mixed, with selective buying supporting the key index to a higher finish, traders said.

"The second board is trending higher. The main board is also healthy as there's no bad news around," said a K&N Kenanga dealer. The re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton was not a market factor as he had been expected to win, traders said.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index rose 2.28 points to 1,179.09.
The Second Board index gained 5.97 points or 0.94 percent to 639.05. It rose as high as 643.34, breaching the November 1 intra-day high of 642.75.
A raft of second boarders hit new highs for the year in intraday dealings -- Trenergy, Belton, Pembinaan YCS, General Lumber, Denko, HIL and MCL.
"The second board index looks like going to 680, 690 in just a short while," said a salesman at a Penang brokerage.
Heavyweights had a mixed day, with Tanjong, Commerce Asset and IJM Corp and AMMB gaining ground, but Genting, EON and Petronas Gas easing off.
